body:
APPLICABLE BEHAVIOUR: the Ordarium 1.3.1 state-change "observation cursor" behaviour — an always-present, opaque, filter-independent durable position whose validation is FAIL-CLOSED (invalid or restored/replaced cursor => InvalidCursorError / code INVALID_CURSOR; never a silent restart). The 1.2.0 commentary behaviour does NOT apply.

WHY (evidence, read-only):
1. The integration's authoritative version declaration is the dependency manifest, and it pins 1.3.1, not 1.2.0:
   - package.json dependencies: @ordarium/core, @ordarium/host-kit, @ordarium/ledger-sqlite = ordarium-v1.3.1 tarballs; devDependency @ordarium/testing = 1.3.1.
   - pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides: all four @ordarium/* entries = ordarium-v1.3.1 tarballs.
   - Installed tree confirms it: node_modules/@ordarium/{core,host-kit,ledger-sqlite}/package.json each report 1.3.1.
2. The observation cursor is Ordarium's state-change feed (ORD-BOOT-0), described in the shipped types as "incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position":
   - node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/state.d.ts / types.d.ts: StateChangeFeed.changes(filter?, cursor?) -> StateChangePage { changes, cursor, hasMore }; unlike the other read surfaces there is no optional nextCursor — "cursor is always present", i.e. an end-of-feed page still yields a durable resume position. The cursor is documented as an "opaque, filter-independent durable position".
   - ledger-sqlite implements it and declares it: capabilities.stateChangeFeed: true (index.d.ts/index.js).
   - Behaviour in code (ledger-sqlite index.js changes()): decodeStateChangeCursor(cursor); then "Semantic validation against the global high-water mark (ORD-BOOT-0.1) ... the cursor is a global, filter-independent position ... Concurrent commits only raise the mark, so a valid cursor cannot be falsely rejected; a restored/replaced ledger lowers it and fails closed" -> throw InvalidCursorError.
   - core errors.d.ts/js: InvalidCursorError -> code INVALID_CURSOR, "refusing to guess a resume point", explicitly distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT and explicitly NOT a silent restart from the beginning of the feed. Capability absence is also fail-closed (LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED) rather than an inferred fallback.
3. The only local source describing the opposite behaviour is docs/release-commentary-1.2.0.md ("predates the incremental state-change feed, so it has no notion of a change-feed cursor and no cursor-invalidation failure. Anything here applies only to the 1.2.0 line" / "Status: historical, superseded by later releases"). It is self-scoped to a line the workspace is not on, and self-declared superseded — so it is not co-applicable to this integration. This is resolved by version scope + explicit supersession, so no peer/boundary query was needed.

STALE PROSE (not the manifest, not controlling): docker/minimal/README.md ("pnpm overrides point ... at the ordarium-v1.2.0 GitHub tarballs"), docs/engineering/audits/CURRENT-STATE-ASSESSMENT.md ("Ordarium pin 1.2.0"), and docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md (r8–r19 all "1.2.0 四行 pin") are dated snapshots written before the 1.3.1 bump registered in the manifest/overrides/installed tree. They agree with the 1.2.0 commentary but are superseded by the current pin.

HONEST SCOPE NOTE: Palimpsest's own code does not call .changes(); the telemetry path (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts) consumes state list pagination (page.nextCursor) plus CAS writes. So the 1.3.1 observation-cursor behaviour governs the capability surface of the pinned dependency the integration is built on; it is not currently exercised by a Palimpsest call site.
